newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of broad EMU slip further - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of broad EMU slip further - JP Morgan.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad-based European monetary union, including Italy, Spain and Sweden, slipped further this week, according to JP Morgan's EMU calculator.
In the past five trading days, market prices indicated that the perceived probabilities of Spain, Sweden, Italy, Denmark and the UK joining EMU in 1999 all slipped lower.

The two largest declines during the week were in Spain, which fell 10.0 percentage points to 64 percent, and in the UK, which fell 14.0 points to 32 percent, the country with the lowest perceived probability of taking part in 1999.
Sweden fell 1.0 point to 64 percent and Italy was down 2.0 points to 61 percent.
According to the calculator, the assigned probabilities of Spain, Sweden, Italy, Denmark and the UK have all declined by between 10 and 21 percentage points over the past month,
The market still believes there is a 100 percent chance of France and Belgium joining in 1999, which was the same as last week, the calculator showed.
JP Morgan's EMU calculator derives from interest rate swaps.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
